src/algorithms/algorithms.c

This file gives the resolver one interface for twelve different scores. It converts distances into similarities and registers each scorer with its name, formula and workspace estimate. It does not choose an acceptance threshold.

Measured observations below describe the recorded dataset and calibrated policy. Timing uses separate synthetic lookup probes; zero observed unsafe matches does not guarantee safety.

Convert edit costs into similarity

Section titled “Convert edit costs into similarity”

lev selects ordinary Levenshtein; osa selects Optimal String Alignment, the restricted adjacent-letter-swap method; dl selects full Damerau-Levenshtein. These adapters call the same dispatcher with different modes. A distance of 1 between names of length 10 becomes 1 - 1/10 = 0.9. Their denominator is the longer normalized name. Inputs are already nonempty, so this division cannot use zero.

Download complete source
1/** @file2 * [PM-Sc4nV8] Adapt every scorer to one rule: larger score means more similar.3 * Edit distances shrink as names improve, so convert d into 1-d/max_length.4 * This table connects a display name to its scorer; the resolver knows no words.5 * osa = Optimal String Alignment (restricted adjacent swaps).6 * dl = full Damerau-Levenshtein; lcs = longest common subsequence.7 * Short adapter names are internal; articles use the expanded names.8 */9#include <ctype.h>10#include <string.h>11#include "pm.h"12static double edit(const Prepared *a, const Property *b, int mode) {13    size_t n = strlen(a->text), m = strlen(b->normalized);14    return 1 - edit_distance(a->text, b->normalized, mode) / (double) (n > m ? n : m);15}1617static double lev(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {18    return edit(a, b, 0);19}2021static double osa(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {22    return edit(a, b, 1);23}2425static double dl(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {26    return edit(a, b, 2);27}28

Normalize weighted costs with weighted lengths

Section titled “Normalize weighted costs with weighted lengths”

Digit edits cost more than letter edits. The denominator must use the same weights. For v1 and v2, each weighted length is 3 and the substitution costs 2, giving a similarity of one third. Using ordinary length here would compare incompatible units.

29static double weighted(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {30    size_t i;31    double n = 0, m = 0;32    for (i = 0; a->text[i]; ++i) n += isdigit((unsigned char)a->text[i]) ? 2 : 1;33    for (i = 0; b->normalized[i]; ++i) m += isdigit((unsigned char)b->normalized[i]) ? 2 : 1;34    return 1 - weighted_distance(a->text, b->normalized) / (n > m ? n : m);35}36

Adapt direct similarities and apply the Winkler bonus

Section titled “Adapt direct similarities and apply the Winkler bonus”

Jaro, longest-common-subsequence, gram and block routines already return similarities. Their adapters pass the prepared character strings through. Winkler is the exception: it adds up to four prefix contributions only when Jaro exceeds 0.7. For Jaro 0.9 and three shared leading letters, the result is 0.93.

Step Calculation
Remaining gap to a perfect score 1 - 0.9 = 0.1
Prefix bonus 3 * 0.1 * 0.1 = 0.03
Adjusted score 0.9 + 0.03 = 0.93

The bonus changes the score, not the decision policy. Similar prefixes can conceal different units or behavior, so the resolver still checks the runner-up margin. NIST describes the prefix preference; the cutoff and four-character limit are explicitly defined by this implementation.

Jaro-Winkler results from this run

Section titled “Jaro-Winkler results from this run”

Run recorded 2026-11-07 11:27 PST. It recovered 126 of 185 typos. It made 1 unsafe acceptances.

Compared with Levenshtein, this policy recovered 48 fewer typos, and used about 3.3 times faster lookups.

A median name lookup took about 19 microseconds with 10 properties and 850 microseconds with 1000. These are separate synthetic typo probes on this host, not timings of the examples below.

Unsafe acceptance: application environment was labeled unknown, but the resolver accepted ApplicationEnvironmentName with score 0.969. Similar spelling did not establish the intended setting.

Rejected typo: default request timeout miliseconds was intended for DefaultRequestTimeoutMilliseconds. That target ranked first at 0.994, but the runner-up scored 0.975. The 0.019 lead was below the required 0.02, so the resolver declined to guess.

Compare methods. Inspect the recorded outcomes.

Shared prefixes can hide important suffixes.43 */44/* measured:ALG06:start - 2026-11-07 recorded run.45 * Recovered 126/185 typos; unsafe accepts 1.46 * Median lookup, 10 properties: about 19 microseconds on this host.47 * Levenshtein recovered 174/185 with 0 unsafe accepts.48 * Input: application environment49 * Outcome: accepted ApplicationEnvironmentName, but input was labeled unknown.50 * Policy limits and comparisons: docs/measured-results.md.51 * measured:ALG06:end */52static double winkler(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {53    double base_similarity = jaro(a, b);54    size_t prefix_length = 0;55    while (prefix_length < 4 && a->text[prefix_length] &&56           a->text[prefix_length] == b->normalized[prefix_length]) ++prefix_length;57    if (base_similarity > 0.7) {58        /* Reward matching starts by a fraction of the remaining gap to 1. */59        double prefix_bonus = (double)prefix_length * 0.1 * (1 - base_similarity);60        return base_similarity + prefix_bonus;61    }62    return base_similarity;63}6465static double lcs(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {66    return lcs_score(a->text, b->normalized);67}6869static double jaccard(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {70    return gram_score(a->text, b->normalized, 0);71}7273static double dice(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {74    return gram_score(a->text, b->normalized, 1);75}7677static double cosine(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {78    return gram_score(a->text, b->normalized, 2);79}8081static double ratcliff(const Prepared *a, const Property *b) {82    return ratcliff_score(a->text, b->normalized);83}84/* ID zero deliberately has no scorer. Exact normalization still runs for all IDs.85 * Workspace values describe bounded arrays, not measured process memory. */

Register scorers without embedding schema rules

Section titled “Register scorers without embedding schema rules”

Array position is the method ID used throughout calibration, evaluation and reporting. Entry zero has a null scorer because exact matching happens in the shared resolver. The metadata describes actual implementations, including the library-dependent sorting cost of qsort. Adding a method also requires updating the method count and correctness tests.
